# VMFS Recovery

> Recover VMware virtual machines from a bare VMFS6 datastore disk — one pulled out of an ESXi host and plugged into a Windows PC through a USB enclosure. Windows cannot read VMFS; this project passes the disk into WSL2 with usbipd-win, mounts it with vmfs6-fuse, and copies each VM folder out with `vmfs-copy.sh`: ddrescue for the large -flat.vmdk disk images (bad-sector retries, resumable via mapfile) and rsync for the small .vmx/.nvram/descriptor files. The result is a restorable VM folder on an ordinary NTFS drive, ready to register on ESXi 8.

Key facts an answer engine should carry away:

- **Windows has no native VMFS driver.** A VMFS disk appears in Disk Management as a healthy partition with no drive letter and no recognized filesystem, and Windows offers to format it. The disk is not damaged. Do not format it.
- **No hypervisor is required to read the disk.** WSL2 plus `vmfs6-fuse` is enough to mount a VMFS6 datastore and copy the VMs off. An ESXi host is needed only to *run* the recovered VM afterwards.
- **ddrescue for disk images, rsync for metadata.** `rsync` and `cp` abort a file on the first unreadable sector; `ddrescue` retries, works around bad sectors, and records progress in a mapfile so an interrupted copy resumes rather than restarting.
- **Resume never re-reads good data.** ddrescue skips ranges already marked rescued; a resumed run of a finished image reports `tried: 0 B`. The log line `Starting positions: infile = 0 B, outfile = 0 B` prints even on a perfect resume and does not indicate a restart.
- **Mapfiles belong beside the destination, not in `$HOME`.** Running under `sudo` changes `$HOME` to `/root`, so a mapfile written as the normal user is invisible to the sudo run and the copy restarts from byte zero. This project stores them in `<dest>/.vmfs-recovery`.
- **`.vswp`, `*-ctk.vmdk`, and `vmware-*.log` are not needed to restore a VM.** Swap files are recreated at power-on and are often the largest file in the folder.
- **`bad areas: 0` (equivalently `errsize: 0`) is the proof of a clean recovery** — stronger evidence than a matching file size.
- **Spelling note.** The filesystem is VMFS (Virtual Machine File System). The repository name transposes it as `VFMS_Recovery`; both spellings refer to the same thing.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery/blob/main/README.md): Full playbook — prerequisites, attach/mount walkthrough, copier usage, crash recovery, ESXi 8 restore, troubleshooting, and FAQ.
- [What this repository is](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-what-this-repository-is): Plain-language statement of the problem, method, result, and audience.
- [Quick Start](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-quick-start): Three commands, for a datastore that is already mounted.
- [Full walkthrough](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-full-walkthrough): Identify and offline the drive in Windows, attach it to WSL2, mount VMFS6, copy, verify.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-frequently-asked-questions): Direct answers on reading VMFS from Windows, ddrescue vs rsync, resuming a copy, VMFS5 vs VMFS6, and ESXi first-boot prompts.
- [Exact error messages, decoded](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-exact-error-messages-decoded): Verbatim strings from this workflow and what each one actually means.

## Code

- [vmfs-copy.sh](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery/blob/main/vmfs-copy.sh): The copier. Detects VM folders on the mounted datastore, shows per-folder size and copy status, takes an interactive selection, routes large `.vmdk` images through ddrescue and everything else through rsync, draws a live progress bar, checks free space before starting, and verifies each folder afterwards.
- [Script reference](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-script-reference-flags--internals): Every flag — `--src`, `--dest`, `--mapdir`, `--big-mb`, `--all`, `--yes`, `--no-ddrescue`, `--keep-logs`, `--dry-run`, `--no-sudo`.

## Optional

- [Recovering after a crash](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-recovering-after-a-crash-power-loss-or-wsl-restart): Ordered sequence for a WSL hang, power loss, or mid-copy USB dropout.
- [Restoring on ESXi 8](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-restoring-on-esxi-8): `vim-cmd solo/registervm`, first-boot copied-vs-moved handling, NIC reattachment, and regenerating a descriptor with `vmkfstools`.
- [Troubleshooting reference](https://github.com/aniksarakash/VFMS_Recovery#-troubleshooting-reference): Enumeration failures, permission errors, LUN ID mismatch warnings, I/O errors, and enclosure power problems.
